punchline: Brown says guilt means "I did something bad" and can be repaired, while shame says "I am bad" and pushes you to hide.
thirty_sec: In The Gifts of Imperfection, Brené Brown separates guilt from shame. Guilt says I did something bad, compares the behavior with our values and makes an apology and repair possible. Shame says I am bad, and her research links it with addiction, aggression and depression. Even apologies show the difference: I made a mistake versus I am a mistake.
